  1521→FETCH_OPCODE:
  1522→	LD A, (XIX)  ; opcode = fetch_byte();
  1523→	INC XIX
  1524→
  1525→	BIT 7, A	; if (opcode & 0x80)
  1526→	JP Z, OPCODE_BIT_7_NOT_SET
  1527→
  1528→	; ====  VIDEO instruction (0x80) ====
  1529→_OPCODE_0x80:
  1530→;		uint16_t offset = ((opcode << 8) | fetch_byte()) * 2;
  1531→	LD W, A
  1532→	LD A, (XIX)
  1533→	INC XIX
  1534→	PUSH WA				; save offset_raw = (opcode << 8) | low_byte
  1535→
  1536→	; Read x from bytecode (XIX still points to bytecode stream)
  1537→	LD D, 0
  1538→	LD E, (XIX)			; x = fetch_byte()
  1539→	INC XIX
  1540→	PUSH DE				; save x
  1541→
  1542→	; Read y from bytecode
  1543→	LD A, (XIX)			; y = fetch_byte()
  1544→	INC XIX
  1545→	LD H, 0
  1546→	LD L, A				; HL = y
  1547→
  1548→	; Save bytecode position (past all 4 consumed bytes: opcode, offset_lo, x, y)
  1549→	PUSH HL				; save y
  1550→	LD XDE, XIX
  1551→	SUB XDE, (CUR_BYTECODE)
  1552→	LD (VM_PC), DE
  1553→	POP HL				; restore y
  1554→
  1555→	; Restore x
  1556→	POP DE				; DE = x
  1557→
  1558→	; Compute offset and set up video data pointer
  1559→	; Opcodes >= 0x80 always use CUR_VIDEO_2 (not CUR_VIDEO_DATA/VIDEO_1)
  1560→	; Reference: vid_opcd_0x80 calls setDataBuffer(_ply, 1) → segVideo2
  1561→	POP WA				; WA = offset_raw
  1562→	SLA 1, WA			; offset *= 2 (uint16_t wraps, e.g. 0x883E*2 → 0x107C)
  1563→	EXTZ XWA
  1564→	LD XIX, (CUR_VIDEO_2)
  1565→	ADD XIX, XWA
  1566→
  1567→;		if (y > 199)

  1570→;			y = 199;
  1571→;		}

  1599→	INC 2, XIX

  1604→	INC XIX

  1613→	BIT 4, B

  1617→	LD E, (XIX)
  1618→	INC XIX
  1619→	JP _0x40_x_done
  1620→
  1621→_0x40_x_var:

  1624→	JP _0x40_x_done
  1625→
  1626→_0x40_x_bit5set:

  1628→	BIT 4, B
  1629→	JP Z, _0x40_x_done
  1630→	; x += 0x100

  1646→

  1648→	JP NZ, _0x40_y_var

1→; (c) 2024 Felipe Correa da Silva Sanches <juca@members.fsf.org>

     3→;
     4→; This is a port of the Another World VM (initially supporting only non-interactive
     5→; playback of the game intro) to run from an extension board on a
     6→; Technics SX-KN5000 musical keyboard.
     7→;
     8→; This program must replace the hd-ae5000_v2_01i.ic4 ROM of the extension board.
     9→;
    10→; This implementation is derived from my port of the Another World VM
    11→; as a high-level emulation on MAME
    12→;
    13→; And that port was derived from Fabien Sanglard's AW-VM available at:
    14→; https://github.com/fabiensanglard/Another-World-Bytecode-Interpreter
    15→;
    16→; The assembler I am using is compiled from source-code downloaded from
    17→; http://john.ccac.rwth-aachen.de:8000/as/index.html
    18→;
    19→; Game assets must be extracted from an original copy of the game
    20→; using the scripts provided at:
    21→; https://github.com/felipesanches/AnotherWorld_VMTools
    22→;
    23→; === EQU Constants (shared) ===
    24→PC_OFFSET			EQU 0  ; 16 bits
    25→REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET	EQU 2  ; 16 bits
    26→INACTIVE_THREAD		EQU 0FFFFh
    27→DELETE_THIS_THREAD	EQU 0FFFEh
    28→NO_REQUEST 			EQU 0FFFFh
    29→TICKS_PER_SLICE		EQU 250		; ~20ms at 12500 Hz tick rate (80 µs/tick)
    30→
    31→CURRENT_STATE	EQU 0  ; boolean stored as a byte
    32→REQUESTED_STATE	EQU 1  ; boolean stored as a byte
    33→
    34→FROZEN	EQU 0
    35→NOT_FROZEN EQU 1
    36→NO_STATE_REQUEST EQU 0FFh
    37→
    38→; These off-screen video pages are stored in external RAM:
    39→; MAINCPU: in DRAM at 0x020000-0x05FFFF
    40→; EXTENSION: in extension board SRAM at 0x240000-0x27FFFF
    41→	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
    42→PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 020000h
    43→PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 030000h
    44→PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 040000h
    45→PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 050000h
    46→	endif
    47→	ifdef TARGET_EXTENSION
    48→PAGE_BITMAP_0 EQU 240000h
    49→PAGE_BITMAP_1 EQU 250000h
    50→PAGE_BITMAP_2 EQU 260000h
    51→PAGE_BITMAP_3 EQU 270000h
    52→	endif
    53→
    54→; VM variable indices (used by the game engine)
    55→VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED		EQU 03Ch
    56→VM_VARIABLE_LAST_KEYCHAR	EQU 0DAh
    57→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_UP_DOWN	EQU 0E5h
    58→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION		EQU 0FAh
    59→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_JUMP_DOWN	EQU 0FBh
    60→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_LEFT_RIGHT	EQU 0FCh
    61→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_MASK	EQU 0FDh
    62→VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION_POS_MASK EQU 0FEh
    63→VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y		EQU 0F9h
    64→
    65→; Game part IDs (from reference: parts.h)

   269→; initForPart: Reset all threads and prepare for a new game part
   270→; Input: WA = partId
   271→initForPart:
   272→	LD (CURRENT_PART_ID), WA
   273→
   274→	; Reset VM state
   275→	LD XIX, VM_STACK
   276→	LD (VM_STACK_POINTER), XIX
   277→
   278→	; Reset all threads: inactive and unfrozen
   279→	LD IX, 0
   280→_initForPart_loop:
   281→	PUSH IX
   282→	SLA 2, IX
   283→	EXTZ XIX
   284→	ADD XIX, THREADS_DATA
   285→	LDW (XIX + PC_OFFSET), INACTIVE_THREAD
   286→	LDW (XIX + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), NO_REQUEST
   287→	POP IX
   288→
   289→	PUSH IX
   290→	SLA 1, IX
   291→	EXTZ XIX
   292→	ADD XIX, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
   293→	LD (XIX + CURRENT_STATE), NOT_FROZEN
   294→	LD (XIX + REQUESTED_STATE), NO_STATE_REQUEST
   295→	POP IX
   296→
   297→	INC IX
   298→	CP IX, 64
   299→	JP NE, _initForPart_loop
   300→
   301→	; Start thread 0 at PC=0
   302→	LDW (THREADS_DATA + PC_OFFSET), 0
   303→
   304→	; Set variable 0xE4 = 0x14 (as per reference)
   305→	LD A, 0E4h
   306→	LD DE, 014h
   307→	CALL _write_vm_var
   308→
   309→	; Load resource pointers from PART_RESOURCE_TABLE
   310→	; Table index = (partId - GAME_PART_FIRST) * 16 (4 DDs per entry)
   311→	LD WA, (CURRENT_PART_ID)
   312→	SUB WA, GAME_PART_FIRST
   313→	; WA = part index (0-9)
   314→	SLA 4, WA			; WA = index * 16
   315→	EXTZ XWA
   316→	ADD XWA, PART_RESOURCE_TABLE
   317→
   318→	; XWA now points to: [palette_ptr, bytecode_ptr, video1_ptr, video2_ptr]
   319→	LD XIX, XWA
   320→	LD XWA, (XIX + 4)	; bytecode pointer
   321→	LD (CUR_BYTECODE), XWA
   322→	LD XWA, (XIX + 8)	; video1 pointer
   323→	LD (CUR_VIDEO_DATA), XWA
   324→	LD (CUR_VIDEO_1), XWA
   325→	LD XWA, (XIX + 12)	; video2 pointer
   326→	LD (CUR_VIDEO_2), XWA
   327→	LD XWA, (XIX + 0)	; palette pointer
   328→	LD (CUR_PALETTES), XWA
   329→	RET

   332→GAME_RESET:
   333→	CALL VIDEO_START
   334→
   335→	; Zero all VM variables (256 x 16-bit = 512 bytes)
   336→	LD XDE, VM_VARIABLES
   337→	LD WA, 0
   338→	LD BC, 256
   339→_zero_vars_loop:
   340→	LD (XDE), WA
   341→	INC 2, XDE
   342→	DJNZ BC, _zero_vars_loop
   343→
   344→	LDB (CURRENT_THREAD), 0
   345→	LDW (VM_PC), 0
   346→	LD XIX, VM_STACK
   347→	LD (VM_STACK_POINTER), XIX
   348→
   349→	; All threads are initially disabled and unfrozen
   350→	LD IX, 0
   351→_setup_threads__loop:
   352→
   353→	PUSH IX
   354→	SLA 2, IX
   355→	EXTZ XIX
   356→	ADD XIX, THREADS_DATA
   357→	LDW (XIX + PC_OFFSET), INACTIVE_THREAD
   358→	LDW (XIX + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), NO_REQUEST
   359→	POP IX
   360→
   361→	PUSH IX
   362→	SLA 1, IX
   363→	EXTZ XIX
   364→	ADD XIX, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
   365→	LD (XIX + CURRENT_STATE), NOT_FROZEN
   366→	LD (XIX + REQUESTED_STATE), NO_STATE_REQUEST
   367→	POP IX
   368→
   369→	INC IX
   370→	CP IX, 64
   371→	JP NE, _setup_threads__loop
   372→
   373→	; Start thread 0 at PC=0 (matching initForPart behavior)
   374→	LDW (THREADS_DATA + PC_OFFSET), 0
   375→
   376→	; Initialize VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED with a fixed seed (no RTC available)
   377→	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED
   378→	LD DE, 1234h			; Fixed seed value
   379→	CALL _write_vm_var
   380→
   381→	; VM_HACK_INIT_VAR_54_WITH_81: Required for Interplay logo display
   382→	LD A, 054h
   383→	LD DE, 0081h
   384→	CALL _write_vm_var
   385→
   386→	; Copy protection bypass: Set the variables that the protection
   387→	; bytecode (resource 0x15) would set when the correct code wheel
   388→	; answer is entered. Without these, the water part's check at
   389→	; subroutine 0x009A kills all threads and the game halts.
   390→	; Protection check requires: var[0xBC] & 0x0010, var[0xF2] == 0x0FA0,
   391→	; var[0xDC] == 0x21. These are set by the protection code at offsets
   392→	; 0x0CCF (OR var[0xBC] |= 0x0010), 0x0D0D (var[0xF2] = 0x0FA0),
   393→	; and indirectly via the VM hack (var[0xDC] = 0x21).
   394→	LD A, 0BCh
   395→	LD DE, 0010h
   396→	CALL _write_vm_var
   397→	LD A, 0F2h
   398→	LD DE, 0FA0h
   399→	CALL _write_vm_var
   400→	LD A, 0DCh
   401→	LD DE, 021h
   402→	CALL _write_vm_var
   403→
   404→	; Initialize part tracking and start from the protection/splash screens
   405→	; (Part 0 = logo, credits, code-wheel). We bypass the code wheel by
   406→	; starting thread 0 at the splash screen entry point (0x007B) instead
   407→	; of PC=0 (which enters the code wheel). We also pre-start the display
   408→	; loop thread and set the frame delay variable, matching what the
   409→	; bytecode's normal entry at 0x0000 would have done.
   410→	LDW (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), 0
   411→	LD WA, GAME_PART_PROTECTION
   412→	CALL initForPart
   413→
   414→	; Override thread 0 PC to splash screen entry (skip code wheel at 0x0000)
   415→	LDW (THREADS_DATA + PC_OFFSET), 007Bh
   416→
   417→	; Start display loop on thread 60 (bytecode address 0x10A3)
   418→	; Thread 60 slot = 60 * 4 = 240 bytes into THREADS_DATA
   419→	LDW (THREADS_DATA + (60 * 4) + PC_OFFSET), 010A3h
   420→
   421→	; Set var[0xFF] = 2 (frame delay, normally set by bytecode at 0x0003)
   422→	LD A, 0FFh
   423→	LD DE, 2
   424→	CALL _write_vm_var
   425→
   426→	RET

   428→ENTRY:
   429→	EI 0 ; Enable interrupts (INTT1 timer ISR)
   430→
   431→	CALL GAME_RESET
   432→
   433→	; Initialize frame start time
   434→	LD XWA, (SYSTEM_TICKS)
   435→	LD (FRAME_START_TICKS), XWA
   436→
   437→MAIN_LOOP:
   438→	CALL EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
   439→	JP MAIN_LOOP
   440→
   441→LONG_PAUSE:
   442→	LD BC, 0
   443→LONG_PAUSE_LOOP1:
   444→	LD DE, 080h
   445→LONG_PAUSE_LOOP2:
   446→	DJNZ DE, LONG_PAUSE_LOOP2
   447→	DJNZ BC, LONG_PAUSE_LOOP1
   448→	RET
   449→
   450→PAUSE:
   451→	; Timer-based frame delay using VM variable 0xFF (pause slices).
   452→	; Each slice = ~20ms. Polls SYSTEM_TICKS until elapsed >= target.
   453→	; DJNZ fallback counter exits if timer ISR doesn't fire.
   454→
   455→	; Read VM variable 0xFF (pause slices)
   456→	LD A, 0FFh
   457→	CALL _read_vm_var		; DE = var[0xFF]
   458→
   459→	; Cap slices at 1-5 range
   460→	LD A, E
   461→	CP A, 0
   462→	JP NE, _pause_nonzero
   463→	LD A, 1
   464→_pause_nonzero:
   465→	CP A, 6
   466→	JP ULT, _pause_capped
   467→	LD A, 5
   468→_pause_capped:
   469→	; Compute target_ticks = slices * TICKS_PER_SLICE
   470→	LD D, 0
   471→	LD E, A					; DE = capped slices (1-5)
   472→	LD WA, TICKS_PER_SLICE	; WA = 250
   473→	MUL XWA, DE			; XWA = target_ticks (16-bit result in WA)
   474→	LD XBC, XWA			; XBC = target_ticks (preserved across loop)
   475→
   476→	; Check for overrun: elapsed already >= target?
   477→	LD XWA, (SYSTEM_TICKS)
   478→	LD XDE, (FRAME_START_TICKS)
   479→	SUB XWA, XDE			; XWA = elapsed ticks
   480→	CP XWA, XBC
   481→	JP UGE, _pause_overrun
   482→
   483→	; Poll timer with DJNZ fallback (65536 iterations ≈ 80ms safety net)
   484→	LD HL, 0				; fallback counter
   485→_pause_wait:
   486→	LD XWA, (SYSTEM_TICKS)
   487→	LD XDE, (FRAME_START_TICKS)
   488→	SUB XWA, XDE			; XWA = elapsed
   489→	CP XWA, XBC
   490→	JP UGE, _pause_done_ok
   491→	DJNZ HL, _pause_wait
   492→	; Fallback expired — exit (timer may not be running)
   493→
   494→_pause_done_ok:
   495→	LD (LAST_FRAME_TICKS), WA
   496→	LDB (FRAME_OVERRAN), 0
   497→	RET
   498→
   499→_pause_overrun:
   500→	LD (LAST_FRAME_TICKS), WA
   501→	LDB (FRAME_OVERRAN), 1
   502→	RET

   899→readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy:
   900→	LD DE, (CUR_ZOOM)	; 16-bit zoom
   901→	;	pt.x -= m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   902→	LD WA, 0
   903→	LD A, (XIX)
   904→	INC XIX
   905→	LD HL, (XSP + 6)
   906→	MUL XWA, DE			; PT.X *= ZOOM
   907→	SRL 2, XWA			; PT.X /= default_zoom (40h): unsigned 32-bit shift by 6
   908→	SRL 4, XWA
   909→	SUB HL, WA
   910→	LD (XSP + 6), HL
   911→
   912→	;	pt.y -= m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   913→	LD WA, 0
   914→	LD A, (XIX)
   915→	INC XIX
   916→	LD HL, (XSP + 4)
   917→	MUL XWA, DE			; PT.Y *= ZOOM
   918→	SRL 2, XWA			; PT.Y /= default_zoom (40h): unsigned 32-bit shift by 6
   919→	SRL 4, XWA
   920→	SUB HL, WA
   921→	LD (XSP + 4), HL
   922→
   923→	ld B, 0
   924→	LD C, (XIX)		; num_children - 1
   925→	INC XIX
   926→	INC BC			; BC = num_children

   928→children_loop:
   929→	LD WA, (XIX); offset 
   930→	INC 2, XIX
   931→	EX W, A
   932→	PUSH WA
   933→	PUSHW (XSP + 8); po.x = pt.x
   934→	PUSHW (XSP + 8); po.y = pt.y
   935→
   936→	; po.x += m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   937→	LD WA, 0
   938→	LD A, (XIX)
   939→	INC XIX
   940→	LD HL, (XSP + 2)
   941→	MUL XWA, DE			; PO.X *= ZOOM
   942→	SRL 2, XWA			; PO.X /= default_zoom (40h): unsigned 32-bit shift by 6
   943→	SRL 4, XWA
   944→	ADD HL, WA
   945→	LD (XSP + 2), HL
   946→	
   947→	; po.y += m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] * zoom / DEFAULT_ZOOM;
   948→	LD WA, 0
   949→	LD A, (XIX)
   950→	INC XIX
   951→	LD HL, (XSP)
   952→	MUL XWA, DE			; PO.Y *= ZOOM
   953→	SRL 2, XWA			; PO.Y /= default_zoom (40h): unsigned 32-bit shift by 6
   954→	SRL 4, XWA
   955→	ADD HL, WA
   956→	LD (XSP), HL
   957→
   958→	PUSH DE			; save zoom
   959→	LD DE, 0FFh				; uint16_t color = 0xFF;
   960→	LD HL, (XSP + 6) ;offset
   961→	AND HL, 8000h
   962→	JP Z, OFFSET_BIT15_NOT_SET
   963→	LD DE, 0
   964→	LD E,(XIX)				; 	color = m_polygonData[m_data_offset++] & 0x7F;
   965→	AND E, 7Fh
   966→	INC 2, XIX				; 	m_data_offset++; //and waste a byte...
   967→OFFSET_BIT15_NOT_SET:
   968→
   969→	PUSH XIX			;	 uint16_t backup = m_data_offset;
   970→	LD XIX, (CUR_VIDEO_DATA)
   971→	LD WA, (XSP + 0Ah) ;offset
   972→	SLA 1, WA		 ; m_data_offset = (offset & 0x7FFF) * 2;
   973→	EXTZ XWA
   974→	ADD XIX, XWA
   975→	
   976→	LD HL, DE
   977→	; here L is the computed new color
   978→	; and BC is the children loop counter
   979→
   980→	; B needs color, DE needs x param
   981→	; zoom is in CUR_ZOOM (memory)
   982→
   983→	LD DE, (XSP + 4)	; restore zoom in DE for next loop iteration
   984→
   985→	PUSH BC
   986→	LD B, L		; color
   987→	LD DE, (XSP + 0ah)		; PO.x
   988→	LD HL, (XSP + 08h)		; PO.y
   989→	; (color, CUR_ZOOM, po)
   990→	CALL readAndDrawPolygon
   991→	POP BC
   992→	POP XIX				; m_data_offset = backup;
   993→	POP DE		; restore zoom
   994→
   995→	ADD XSP, 6 ; local vars offset, po.x, po.y (INC only supports 1,2,4,8)
   996→	DJNZ BC, children_loop
   997→	RET

  1000→LOAD_SCREEN:
  1001→; Input: XHL = pointer to 32000 bytes of 4bpp Amiga planar screen data
  1002→; Converts to 8bpp chunky and writes 64000 bytes to PAGE_BITMAP_0
  1003→; Planar format: 4 bitplanes x 8000 bytes (320x200 / 8 bits per byte)
  1004→; Each source byte produces 8 destination pixels.
  1005→; Clobbers: XWA, XBC, XDE, XHL; preserves XIX
  1006→	PUSH XIX
  1007→
  1008→	LD (BMP_SRC_PTR), XHL		; save source base pointer
  1009→	LD XDE, PAGE_BITMAP_0		; destination: page 0 buffer
  1010→	LD IX, 8000					; outer loop: 8000 byte positions
  1011→
  1012→_bmp_outer:
  1013→	; Load one byte from each of the 4 bitplanes
  1014→	LD XHL, (BMP_SRC_PTR)
  1015→	LD A, (XHL)					; plane 0 (bit 0 of pixel color)
  1016→	PUSH XHL
  1017→	ADD XHL, 8000
  1018→	LD B, (XHL)					; plane 1 (bit 1)
  1019→	ADD XHL, 8000
  1020→	LD C, (XHL)					; plane 2 (bit 2)
  1021→	ADD XHL, 8000
  1022→	LD W, (XHL)					; plane 3 (bit 3)
  1023→	POP XHL
  1024→	INC XHL
  1025→	LD (BMP_SRC_PTR), XHL		; advance source pointer
  1026→
  1027→	; Convert 8 pixels from MSB to LSB
  1028→	; A=plane0, B=plane1, C=plane2, W=plane3
  1029→	LD H, 8						; pixel counter (8 pixels per byte)
  1030→_bmp_pixel:
  1031→	LD L, 0
  1032→	; Extract MSB from each plane (p3 first → bit 3 of pixel)
  1033→	SLA 1, W					; plane 3 MSB → carry
  1034→	RLC L						; carry → L bit 0
  1035→	SLA 1, C					; plane 2 MSB → carry
  1036→	RLC L						; carry → L bit 0, prev → bit 1
  1037→	SLA 1, B					; plane 1 MSB → carry
  1038→	RLC L						; carry → L bit 0
  1039→	SLA 1, A					; plane 0 MSB → carry
  1040→	RLC L						; L = (p3<<3)|(p2<<2)|(p1<<1)|p0
  1041→	LD (XDE), L
  1042→	INC XDE
  1043→	DJNZ H, _bmp_pixel
  1044→
  1045→	DJNZ IX, _bmp_outer
  1046→
  1047→	POP XIX
  1048→	RET
  1049→
  1050→SETUP_PALETTE:
  1051→	; WA: palette index (0-63), already extracted by caller (opcode 0x0B does SRA 8)
  1052→	; XWA: zero-extended by caller (EXTZ XWA)
  1053→	; Palette format: 2 bytes per color, 0x0RGB (4 bits per channel)
  1054→	; Byte 0: 0000_RRRR (low nibble = red)
  1055→	; Byte 1: GGGG_BBBB (high nibble = green, low nibble = blue)
  1056→
  1057→	; Compute byte offset: palette_index * 32
  1058→	SLA 1, WA			; * 2
  1059→	SLA 4, WA			; * 16 → total * 32 (each palette = 16 colors × 2 bytes)
  1060→	LD XHL, (CUR_PALETTES)
  1061→	ADD XHL, XWA		; XHL = palette data pointer
  1062→
  1063→	; Set VGA DAC write index to 0
  1064→	; (Write_VGA_Register preserves XHL, XIX, XIY, BC)
  1065→	LDW WA, 3c8h
  1066→	LDW BC, 0
  1067→	CALR Write_VGA_Register
  1068→
  1069→	PUSH XIX
  1070→	LD XIX, 16			; loop counter (XIX preserved by Write_VGA_Register)
  1071→
  1072→PALETTE_LOOP:
  1073→	; red: low nibble of byte 0
  1074→	LD A, (XHL)
  1075→	AND A, 0Fh
  1076→	LD C, A				; MN89304 DAC is 4-bit (0-15), no scaling needed
  1077→	LDW WA, 3c9h
  1078→	CALR Write_VGA_Register
  1079→	INC XHL
  1080→
  1081→	; green: high nibble of byte 1
  1082→	LD A, (XHL)
  1083→	SRL 4, A			; logical shift right to extract high nibble
  1084→	LD C, A
  1085→	LDW WA, 3c9h
  1086→	CALR Write_VGA_Register
  1087→
  1088→	; blue: low nibble of byte 1
  1089→	LD A, (XHL)
  1090→	AND A, 0Fh
  1091→	LD C, A
  1092→	LDW WA, 3c9h
  1093→	CALR Write_VGA_Register
  1094→	INC XHL
  1095→
  1096→	DEC 1, XIX
  1097→	CP IX, 0
  1098→	JP NE, PALETTE_LOOP
  1099→	POP XIX
  1100→	RET

  1234→; _read_vm_var: Read vm_variable[A] into DE
  1235→; Input: A = variable index (0-255)

  1240→	SLA 1, WA
  1241→	EXTZ XWA
  1242→	LD XIY, VM_VARIABLES

  1261→; _cpanel_send_byte: Send/receive one byte via SC1 synchronous I/O
  1262→; In sync mode, writing SC1BUF simultaneously sends and receives.
  1263→; Input: A = byte to send
  1264→; Output: A = byte received
  1265→; Clobbers: A only (W preserved)
  1266→_cpanel_send_byte:
  1267→	LD (SC1BUF), A			; Start 8-bit transfer
  1268→	LD A, 0FFh				; Delay ~255 iterations (~95µs at 16 MHz > 64µs @ 125 kHz effective SCLK)
  1269→.delay:
  1270→	DEC 1, A
  1271→	JR NZ, .delay
  1272→	LD A, (SC1BUF)			; Read received byte
  1273→	RET

  1275→; _cpanel_query_segment: Query a control panel button segment
  1276→; Input: B = command (0x20=left panel, 0xE0=right panel), C = segment number
  1277→; Output: A = button bitmap
  1278→; Clobbers: A, W
  1279→_cpanel_query_segment:

  1281→	CALL _cpanel_send_byte
  1282→	LD A, C					; Send segment byte
  1283→	CALL _cpanel_send_byte
  1284→	LD A, 0FFh				; Send dummy (clock in header)
  1285→	CALL _cpanel_send_byte	; A = header (discard)
  1286→	LD A, 0FFh				; Send dummy (clock in bitmap)
  1287→	CALL _cpanel_send_byte	; A = button bitmap

  1291→INPUT_UPDATE_PLAYER:
  1292→	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
  1293→	; Query CPR_SEG4 (right panel segment 4) for direction buttons
  1294→	; CPR_SEG4: bit1=UP(PART:RIGHT2), bit4=LEFT(CONDUCTOR:LEFT),
  1295→	;           bit5=DOWN(CONDUCTOR:RIGHT2), bit6=RIGHT(CONDUCTOR:RIGHT1)
  1296→	LD B, 0E0h				; Right panel command
  1297→	LD C, 004h				; Segment 4
  1298→	CALL _cpanel_query_segment
  1299→	LD H, A					; H = CPR_SEG4 bitmap
  1300→
  1301→	; Query CPL_SEG4 (left panel segment 4) for action button
  1302→	; CPL_SEG4: bit3=ACTION(VARIATION 4)
  1303→	LD B, 020h				; Left panel command
  1304→	; C still = 004h
  1305→	CALL _cpanel_query_segment
  1306→	LD L, A					; L = CPL_SEG4 bitmap
  1307→
  1308→	; Build lr (left/right), ud (up/down), and mask m
  1309→	; H, L, C are preserved across _write_vm_var (only clobbers XIY, XWA)
  1310→	LD C, 0					; C = mask accumulator (m)
  1311→
  1312→	; --- RIGHT (H bit 6 = CONDUCTOR:RIGHT1) ---
  1313→	LD DE, 0				; lr = 0
  1314→	BIT 6, H
  1315→	JR Z, .no_right
  1316→	LD DE, 1				; lr = 1
  1317→	SET 0, C				; m |= 1 (right)
  1318→.no_right:
  1319→
  1320→	; --- LEFT (H bit 4 = CONDUCTOR:LEFT) ---
  1321→	BIT 4, H
  1322→	JR Z, .no_left
  1323→	LD DE, -1				; lr = -1
  1324→	SET 1, C				; m |= 2 (left)
  1325→.no_left:
  1326→
  1327→	; Write VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_LEFT_RIGHT = lr (DE)
  1328→	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_LEFT_RIGHT
  1329→	CALL _write_vm_var
  1330→
  1331→	; --- DOWN (H bit 5 = CONDUCTOR:RIGHT2) ---
  1332→	LD DE, 0				; ud = 0
  1333→	BIT 5, H
  1334→	JR Z, .no_down
  1335→	LD DE, 1				; ud = 1
  1336→	SET 2, C				; m |= 4 (down)
  1337→.no_down:
  1338→
  1339→	; --- UP (H bit 1 = PART:RIGHT2) ---
  1340→	BIT 1, H
  1341→	JR Z, .no_up
  1342→	LD DE, -1				; ud = -1
  1343→	SET 3, C				; m |= 8 (up)
  1344→	; UP pressed: write HERO_POS_UP_DOWN = -1
  1345→	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_UP_DOWN
  1346→	CALL _write_vm_var		; DE = -1
  1347→	JR .up_down_done
  1348→.no_up:
  1349→	; UP not pressed: write HERO_POS_UP_DOWN = ud (0 or 1)
  1350→	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_UP_DOWN
  1351→	CALL _write_vm_var		; DE = ud
  1352→
  1353→.up_down_done:
  1354→	; Write VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_JUMP_DOWN = ud (DE still = ud)
  1355→	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_JUMP_DOWN
  1356→	CALL _write_vm_var
  1357→
  1358→	; Write VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_MASK = m
  1359→	LD D, 0
  1360→	LD E, C					; DE = m (zero-extended)
  1361→	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_MASK
  1362→	CALL _write_vm_var
  1363→
  1364→	; --- ACTION (L bit 3 = VARIATION 4) ---
  1365→	LD DE, 0				; button = 0
  1366→	BIT 3, L
  1367→	JR Z, .no_action
  1368→	LD DE, 1				; button = 1
  1369→	SET 7, C				; m |= 0x80 (action)
  1370→.no_action:
  1371→
  1372→	; Write VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION = button
  1373→	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION
  1374→	CALL _write_vm_var
  1375→
  1376→	; Write VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION_POS_MASK = m (with action bit)
  1377→	LD D, 0
  1378→	LD E, C					; DE = m
  1379→	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION_POS_MASK
  1380→	CALL _write_vm_var
  1381→
  1382→	RET
  1383→
  1384→	else ; TARGET_EXTENSION
  1385→	RET
  1386→	endif

  1390→
  1391→	; Check if a part switch has been requested
  1392→	LD WA, (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART)
  1393→	CP WA, 0
  1394→	JP EQ, _no_part_switch
  1395→
  1396→	; Validate part ID range before switching
  1397→	CP WA, GAME_PART_FIRST
  1398→	JP ULT, _invalid_part_switch
  1399→	CP WA, GAME_PART_LAST
  1400→	JP UGT, _invalid_part_switch
  1401→
  1402→	; Part switch requested - call initForPart (WA = partId)
  1403→	CALL initForPart
  1404→_invalid_part_switch:
  1405→	LDW (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), 0
  1406→_no_part_switch:
  1407→
  1408→	LD A, 0
  1409→_check_thread_reqs__loop:
  1410→
  1411→	; thread->state = thread->requested_state;
  1412→	; After applying, clear requested_state to NOT_FROZEN.
  1413→	; This matches the reference HLE where requested_state is a bool
  1414→	; and "= NO_REQUEST" (0xFFFF) truncates to true (UNFROZEN).
  1415→	; Effect: FREEZE is one-shot (lasts one frame, then auto-unfreezes).
  1416→	; This is critical for the death handler which FREEZEs all threads
  1417→	; then sets up threads 0 and 60 — without auto-unfreeze, they
  1418→	; stay frozen and the password display never runs.
  1419→	PUSH WA
  1420→	SLA 1, WA
  1421→	EXTZ XWA
  1422→	ADD XWA, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
  1423→	LD E, (XWA + REQUESTED_STATE)
  1424→	CP E, NO_STATE_REQUEST
  1425→	JP EQ, _no_state_request
  1426→	LD (XWA + CURRENT_STATE), E
  1427→	LD (XWA + REQUESTED_STATE), NOT_FROZEN	; clear request (auto-unfreeze)
  1428→_no_state_request:
  1429→	POP WA
  1430→
  1431→	PUSH WA
  1432→	SLA 2, WA
  1433→	EXTZ XWA
  1434→	ADD XWA, THREADS_DATA
  1435→	LD DE, (XWA + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET)
  1436→	POP WA
  1437→	CP DE, NO_REQUEST
  1438→	JP EQ, _check_thread_reqs__next_loop
  1439→
  1440→	PUSH WA
  1441→	SLA 2, WA
  1442→	EXTZ XWA
  1443→	ADD XWA, THREADS_DATA
  1444→	LD BC, (XWA + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET)
  1445→	CP DE, DELETE_THIS_THREAD
  1446→	JP NE, _dont_delete_this_thread
  1447→	LD BC, INACTIVE_THREAD
  1448→_dont_delete_this_thread:
  1449→	LDW (XWA + PC_OFFSET), BC
  1450→	LDW (XWA + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), NO_REQUEST
  1451→	POP WA
  1452→
  1453→_check_thread_reqs__next_loop:
  1454→	INC A
  1455→	CP A, 64
  1456→	JP NE, _check_thread_reqs__loop
  1457→
  1458→_end_of__check_thread_reqs:
  1459→	RET

  1462→NEXT_THREAD:

  1513→EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION:
  1514→	PUSH XIX
  1515→	PUSH XIY
  1516→
  1517→	LD IX, (VM_PC)
  1518→	EXTZ XIX
  1519→	ADD XIX, (CUR_BYTECODE)
  1520→
  1521→FETCH_OPCODE:
  1522→	LD A, (XIX)  ; opcode = fetch_byte();
  1523→	INC XIX
  1524→
  1525→	BIT 7, A	; if (opcode & 0x80)
  1526→	JP Z, OPCODE_BIT_7_NOT_SET
  1527→
  1528→	; ====  VIDEO instruction (0x80) ====
  1529→_OPCODE_0x80:
  1530→;		uint16_t offset = ((opcode << 8) | fetch_byte()) * 2;
  1531→	LD W, A
  1532→	LD A, (XIX)
  1533→	INC XIX
  1534→	PUSH WA				; save offset_raw = (opcode << 8) | low_byte
  1535→
  1536→	; Read x from bytecode (XIX still points to bytecode stream)
  1537→	LD D, 0
  1538→	LD E, (XIX)			; x = fetch_byte()
  1539→	INC XIX
  1540→	PUSH DE				; save x
  1541→
  1542→	; Read y from bytecode
  1543→	LD A, (XIX)			; y = fetch_byte()
  1544→	INC XIX
  1545→	LD H, 0
  1546→	LD L, A				; HL = y
  1547→
  1548→	; Save bytecode position (past all 4 consumed bytes: opcode, offset_lo, x, y)
  1549→	PUSH HL				; save y
  1550→	LD XDE, XIX
  1551→	SUB XDE, (CUR_BYTECODE)
  1552→	LD (VM_PC), DE
  1553→	POP HL				; restore y
  1554→
  1555→	; Restore x
  1556→	POP DE				; DE = x
  1557→
  1558→	; Compute offset and set up video data pointer
  1559→	; Opcodes >= 0x80 always use CUR_VIDEO_2 (not CUR_VIDEO_DATA/VIDEO_1)
  1560→	; Reference: vid_opcd_0x80 calls setDataBuffer(_ply, 1) → segVideo2
  1561→	POP WA				; WA = offset_raw
  1562→	SLA 1, WA			; offset *= 2 (uint16_t wraps, e.g. 0x883E*2 → 0x107C)
  1563→	EXTZ XWA
  1564→	LD XIX, (CUR_VIDEO_2)
  1565→	ADD XIX, XWA
  1566→
  1567→;		if (y > 199)
  1568→;		{
  1569→;			x += (y - 199);
  1570→;			y = 199;
  1571→;		}
  1572→	CP HL, 199
  1573→	JP ULE, _0x80_y_ok	; if y <= 199, skip (normal case)
  1574→	; y > 199: adjust coordinates
  1575→	ADD DE, HL
  1576→	SUB DE, 199			; x += (y - 199)
  1577→	LD HL, 199			; y = 199
  1578→_0x80_y_ok:
  1579→
  1580→	LDW (CUR_ZOOM), 040h	; default zoom
  1581→	LD B, 0FFh				; color = BLACK
  1582→	CALL readAndDrawPolygon
  1583→
  1584→	JP _after_PC_update
  1585→
  1586→OPCODE_BIT_7_NOT_SET:
  1587→	BIT 6, A	; if (opcode & 0x40)
  1588→	JP Z, OPCODE_BIT_6_NOT_SET
  1589→
  1590→	; ====  VIDEO instruction (0x40) ====
  1591→_OPCODE_0x40:
  1592→	; A = opcode (bit 6 set), save for bit testing
  1593→	LD B, A
  1594→
  1595→	; offset = fetch_word() * 2 (big-endian)
  1596→	LD WA, (XIX)
  1597→	EX W, A				; byte-swap
  1598→	SLA 1, WA			; offset *= 2
  1599→	INC 2, XIX
  1600→	PUSH WA				; save offset [stack: offset]
  1601→
  1602→	; x = fetch_byte()
  1603→	LD A, (XIX)
  1604→	INC XIX
  1605→	LD D, 0
  1606→	LD E, A				; DE = x (byte value)
  1607→
  1608→	; X addressing mode based on opcode bits 5,4
  1609→	BIT 5, B
  1610→	JP NZ, _0x40_x_bit5set
  1611→
  1612→	; bit 5 clear: extended x
  1613→	BIT 4, B
  1614→	JP NZ, _0x40_x_var
  1615→	; x = (x << 8) | fetch_byte() - 16-bit immediate
  1616→	LD D, E
  1617→	LD E, (XIX)
  1618→	INC XIX
  1619→	JP _0x40_x_done
  1620→
  1621→_0x40_x_var:
  1622→	; x = read_vm_variable(x) - A still has x
  1623→	CALL _read_vm_var	; DE = vm_var[x]
  1624→	JP _0x40_x_done
  1625→
  1626→_0x40_x_bit5set:
  1627→	; bit 5 set
  1628→	BIT 4, B
  1629→	JP Z, _0x40_x_done
  1630→	; x += 0x100
  1631→	ADD DE, 100h
  1632→
  1633→_0x40_x_done:
  1634→	; DE = x
  1635→	PUSH DE				; save x [stack: x, offset]
  1636→
  1637→	; y = fetch_byte()
  1638→	LD A, (XIX)
  1639→	INC XIX
  1640→	LD H, 0
  1641→	LD L, A				; HL = y (byte value)
  1642→
  1643→	; Y addressing mode based on opcode bits 3,2
  1644→	BIT 3, B
  1645→	JP NZ, _0x40_y_done
  1646→
  1647→	BIT 2, B
  1648→	JP NZ, _0x40_y_var
  1649→	; y = (y << 8) | fetch_byte() - 16-bit immediate
  1650→	LD H, L
  1651→	LD L, (XIX)
  1652→	INC XIX
  1653→	JP _0x40_y_done
  1654→
  1655→_0x40_y_var:
  1656→	; y = read_vm_variable(y) - A still has y
  1657→	CALL _read_vm_var	; DE = vm_var[y]
  1658→	LD HL, DE			; HL = y
  1659→
  1660→_0x40_y_done:
  1661→	; HL = y
  1662→	PUSH HL				; save y [stack: y, x, offset]
  1663→
  1664→	; Zoom mode based on opcode bits 1,0
  1665→	LDW (CUR_ZOOM), 040h		; default zoom (16-bit)
  1666→	LD A, B
  1667→	AND A, 3
  1668→
  1669→	CP A, 0
  1670→	JP EQ, _0x40_zoom_done
  1671→
  1672→	CP A, 1
  1673→	JP NE, _0x40_zoom_not_1
  1674→	; zoom = read_vm_variable(fetch_byte())
  1675→	LD A, (XIX)
  1676→	INC XIX
  1677→	CALL _read_vm_var	; DE = vm_var[A]
  1678→	LD (CUR_ZOOM), DE	; zoom = full 16-bit variable value
  1679→	JP _0x40_zoom_done
  1680→
  1681→_0x40_zoom_not_1:
  1682→	CP A, 2
  1683→	JP NE, _0x40_zoom_case3
  1684→	; case 2: zoom = fetch_byte() (literal zoom value)
  1685→	LD WA, 0
  1686→	LD A, (XIX)
  1687→	INC XIX
  1688→	LD (CUR_ZOOM), WA	; zoom = byte, zero-extended to 16-bit
  1689→	JP _0x40_zoom_done
  1690→
  1691→_0x40_zoom_case3:
  1692→	; case 3: m_useVideo2 = true, zoom = 0x40
  1693→	PUSH XWA
  1694→	LD XWA, (CUR_VIDEO_2)
  1695→	LD (CUR_VIDEO_DATA), XWA
  1696→	POP XWA
  1697→
  1698→_0x40_zoom_done:
  1699→	; CUR_ZOOM = 16-bit zoom value
  1700→
  1701→	; Save bytecode position (all variable-length bytes consumed)
  1702→	LD XDE, XIX
  1703→	SUB XDE, (CUR_BYTECODE)
  1704→	LD (VM_PC), DE
  1705→
  1706→	; Restore parameters from stack
  1707→	POP HL				; HL = y
  1708→	POP DE				; DE = x
  1709→	POP WA				; WA = offset
  1710→
  1711→	; Set up polygon data pointer
  1712→	EXTZ XWA
  1713→	LD XIX, (CUR_VIDEO_DATA)
  1714→	ADD XIX, XWA
  1715→
  1716→	; B = color (0xFF = BLACK), zoom in CUR_ZOOM
  1717→	LD B, 0FFh
  1718→
  1719→	; DE = x, HL = y, B = color, XIX = data pointer, CUR_ZOOM = zoom
  1720→	CALL readAndDrawPolygon
  1721→
  1722→	; Reset video data pointer to default (VIDEO_1)
  1723→	PUSH XWA
  1724→	LD XWA, (CUR_VIDEO_1)
  1725→	LD (CUR_VIDEO_DATA), XWA
  1726→	POP XWA
  1727→
  1728→	JP _after_PC_update
  1729→
  1730→OPCODE_BIT_6_NOT_SET:
  1731→
  1732→
  1733→	; ====  MOV CONST instruction  ====
  1734→	CP A, 0
  1735→	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_MOVCONST
  1736→	LD WA, 0
  1737→	LD A, (XIX)		; uint8_t variableId = fetch_byte();
  1738→	INC XIX
  1739→	; Calculate destination pointer first
  1740→	LD XIY, VM_VARIABLES
  1741→	SLA 1, WA
  1742→	EXTZ XWA
  1743→	ADD XIY, XWA
  1744→	; Now fetch the 16-bit value (big-endian bytecode)
  1745→	LD WA, (XIX)	; int16_t value = fetch_word();
  1746→	EX W, A			; byte-swap: bytecode is big-endian
  1747→	INC 2, XIX
  1748→	LD (XIY), WA	; write_vm_variable(variableId, value);
  1749→	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
  1750→INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_MOVCONST:
  1751→
  1752→
  1753→	; ====  MOV instruction  ====
  1754→	CP A, 1
  1755→	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_MOV
  1756→	LD WA, 0
  1757→	LD A, (XIX)		; uint8_t dstVariableId = fetch_byte();
  1758→	INC XIX
  1759→	PUSH WA			; save dstVariableId
  1760→	LD WA, 0
  1761→	LD A, (XIX)		; uint8_t srcVariableId = fetch_byte();
  1762→	INC XIX
  1763→	LD XIY, VM_VARIABLES
  1764→	SLA 1, WA
  1765→	EXTZ XWA
  1766→	ADD XIY, XWA
  1767→	LD DE, (XIY)	; value = read_vm_variable(srcVariableId);
  1768→	; Recalculate XIY for destination variable
  1769→	POP WA			; restore dstVariableId
  1770→	LD XIY, VM_VARIABLES
  1771→	SLA 1, WA
  1772→	EXTZ XWA
  1773→	ADD XIY, XWA
  1774→	LD (XIY), DE	; write_vm_variable(dstVariableId, value);
  1775→	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
  1776→INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_MOV:

1→; =============================================================================
     2→; main.asm - Another World VM for KN5000
     3→; =============================================================================
     4→; Unified platform wrapper for dual-target build:
     5→;   - TARGET_MAINCPU: Standalone main CPU ROM (0xE00000, for MAME testing)
     6→;   - TARGET_EXTENSION: HDAE5000 extension board ROM (0x280000)
     7→;
     8→; Build: make maincpu  OR  make extension
     9→;
    10→; Target: TMP94C241F (TLCS-900/H2) @ 16 MHz
    11→; =============================================================================
    12→
    13→	cpu 96c141		; TLCS-900/H target
    14→	page 0
    15→	maxmode on
    16→
    17→; =============================================================================
    18→; Include shared definitions from kn5000-roms-disasm
    19→; =============================================================================
    20→	include "sfr_tmp94c241.asm"
    21→	include "vga_constants.asm"
    22→	include "tmp94c241.inc"
    23→
    24→; Local macros not in the disasm repo
    25→	include "local_macros.inc"
    26→
    27→; =============================================================================
    28→; RAM Section (target-specific base address)
    29→; =============================================================================
    30→; MAINCPU:   Uses 1MB DRAM at 0x000000-0x0FFFFF (stack in 0x000-0xFFF)
    31→; EXTENSION: Uses 512KB extension board SRAM at 0x200000-0x27FFFF
    32→	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
    33→	ORG 010000h
    34→	endif
    35→	ifdef TARGET_EXTENSION
    36→	ORG 0200000h
    37→	endif
    38→
    39→VM_VARIABLES:	DW	256 DUP (?)
    40→
    41→THREADS_DATA:	DW	64*2 DUP (?)  ; For each of the 64 threads:
    42→
    43→VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE:	DB	64*2 DUP (?)   ; For each of the 64 threads:
    44→
    45→CURRENT_THREAD: DB ?
    46→VM_PC:				DW ?
    47→VM_STACK_POINTER: DD ?
    48→VM_STACK: DW 256 DUP (?)
    49→
    50→POLYGON_NUM_POINTS:	DB ?
    51→POLYGON_BBOX_W:		DW ?					; uint16_t
    52→POLYGON_BBOX_H:		DW ?					; uint16_t
    53→POLYGON_POINTS:		DW	50 DUP (?, ?, ?)
    54→POLYGON_XMIN:	DW ?						; int16_t
    55→POLYGON_XMAX:	DW ?						; int16_t
    56→POLYGON_YMIN:	DW ?						; int16_t
    57→POLYGON_YMAX:	DW ?						; int16_t
    58→HLINEY:		DW ?							; int16_t
    59→CUR_LINE:			; uint32_t
    60→CUR_LINE_LOW:	DW ?
    61→CUR_LINE_HIGH:	DW ?
    62→
    63→CPT1:				; uint32_t
    64→CPT1_LOW:	DW ?
    65→CPT1_HIGH:	DW ?
    66→
    67→CPT2:				; uint32_t
    68→CPT2_LOW:	DW ?
    69→CPT2_HIGH:	DW ?
    70→
    71→STEP1:				; int32_t
    72→STEP1_LOW:	DW ?
    73→STEP1_HIGH:	DW ?
    74→
    75→STEP2:				; int32_t
    76→STEP2_LOW:	DW ?
    77→STEP2_HIGH:	DW ?
    78→
    79→; int16_t x1, x2;
    80→X1:			DW ?
    81→X2:			DW ?
    82→
    83→; 	uint16_t h;
    84→POLYGON_H:	DW ?
    85→DX:			DW ?	; int16_t
    86→
    87→;	int16_t xmax, xmin
    88→LINE_XMIN:	DW ?
    89→LINE_XMAX:	DW ?
    90→CUR_PAGE_PTR_1: DD ?
    91→CUR_PAGE_PTR_2: DD ?
    92→CUR_PAGE_PTR_3: DD ?
    93→CUR_VIDEO_DATA: DD ?			; Pointer to current video polygon data (video1 or video2)
    94→CUR_VIDEO_1: DD ?				; Pointer to current part's video1 data (for reset after video2 use)
    95→CUR_VIDEO_2: DD ?				; Pointer to current part's video2 data (0 if none)
    96→CUR_BYTECODE: DD ?				; Pointer to current part's bytecode
    97→CUR_PALETTES: DD ?				; Pointer to current part's palette data
    98→CUR_ZOOM: DW ?					; uint16_t zoom for polygon scaling (default 0x40)
    99→
   100→STRING_X0: DW ?
   101→
   102→SYSTEM_TICKS:        DD ?		; 32-bit tick counter (ISR-incremented, 12500 Hz)
   103→FRAME_START_TICKS:   DD ?		; Tick count at frame start
   104→LAST_FRAME_TICKS:    DW ?		; Elapsed ticks of last frame (for diagnostics)
   105→FRAME_OVERRAN:       DB ?		; 1 if last frame exceeded budget, 0 otherwise
   106→
   107→REQUESTED_NEXT_PART: DW ?		; Part switch request (0 = no request)
   108→CURRENT_PART_ID: DW ?			; Current game part ID
   109→
   110→BMP_SRC_PTR: DD ?				; Temp: LOAD_SCREEN source pointer during 4bpp conversion
   111→
   112→; =============================================================================
   113→; Main CPU ROM Layout
   114→; =============================================================================
   115→	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
   116→
   117→STACK_TOP		EQU 001000h	; Stack in internal RAM
   118→OFFSCREEN_BUFFER_1	EQU 060000h	; Offscreen buffer (required by vga_init, in DRAM)
   119→
   120→	ORG 0E00000h
   121→
   122→; Fill with 0xFF until code section
   123→	rept 0F0000h		; ~960KB of padding
   124→	db 0FFh
   125→	endm
   126→
   127→	ORG 0EF0000h
   128→
   129→; Jump to Reset_Handler (VGA code is included first for macro definitions)
   130→	jp Reset_Handler
   131→
   132→; Include shared VGA I/O and initialization routines
   133→	include "vga_io.asm"
   134→	include "vga_init.asm"
   135→	ret			; VGA_Setup has no ret (designed for inline use)
   136→
   137→; Entry Point - Called after hardware reset
   138→Reset_Handler:
   139→	include "boot_hw_init.asm"
   140→
   141→	; Set up stack pointer (after hardware init)
   142→	LDA_XWA_IMM24 STACK_TOP
   143→	ld XSP, XWA
   144→
   145→	; Initialize VGA display using shared code
   146→	CALR VGA_Setup
   147→
   148→	; Turn screen on (sequencer clocking mode)
   149→	VGA_SEQUENCER 01h, 001h
   150→
   151→	jp ENTRY
   152→
   153→	endif ; TARGET_MAINCPU
   154→
   155→; =============================================================================
   156→; Extension Board ROM Layout
   157→; =============================================================================
   158→	ifdef TARGET_EXTENSION
   159→
   160→	ORG 0280000h
   161→
   162→EXTENSION_HEADER:
   163→	db 'XAPR'
   164→	dd POINTERS
   165→	JP ENTRY
   166→POINTERS:
   167→	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
   168→	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
   169→	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
   170→	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
   171→	db 0Eh, 00h, 00h, 00h; EMPTY_ROUTINE
   172→
   173→	endif ; TARGET_EXTENSION
   174→
   175→; =============================================================================
   176→; VM Code (shared between both targets)
   177→; =============================================================================
   178→	include "another_world_vm.asm"
   179→
   180→; =============================================================================
   181→; ROM End (target-specific)
   182→; =============================================================================
   183→	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
   184→
   185→INTT1_Handler:
   186→	PUSH XWA
   187→	LD XWA, (SYSTEM_TICKS)
   188→	INC 1, XWA
   189→	LD (SYSTEM_TICKS), XWA
   190→	POP XWA
   191→	RETI
   192→
   193→Default_Handler:
   194→	halt
   195→	jr Default_Handler
   196→
   197→; Reset Handler Location
   198→	ORG 0FFFEE0h
   199→Reset_Entry:
   200→	jp Reset_Handler
   201→
   202→; Fill gap between reset entry and vector table
   203→	ORG 0FFFEE4h
   204→	rept 01Ch
   205→	db 0FFh
   206→	endm
   207→
   208→; Interrupt Vector Table
   209→	ORG 0FFFF00h
   210→VECTOR_TABLE:
   211→	dd 00FFFEE0h		; Vector 0: Reset
   212→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 1
   213→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 2
   214→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 3
   215→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 4
   216→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 5
   217→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 6
   218→	dd Default_Handler	; Vector 7
   219→
   220→	rept 13				; Entries 8-20 (offsets 0x20-0x50)
   221→	dd Default_Handler
   222→	endm
   223→	dd INTT1_Handler		; Entry 21 (offset 0x54): INTT1

1→# Code Review: KN5000 Another World VM Port
     2→
     3→## Comparison with reference MAME HLE implementation
     4→
     5→Reference commit: https://github.com/felipesanches/mame/commit/7cbb93bc3ee05f5ffdd083081530ac0daa2dfa84
     6→
     7→### Fully Implemented
     8→- **Opcode 0x00** (movConst) - OK
     9→- **Opcode 0x04** (CALL) - OK
    10→- **Opcode 0x05** (RET) - OK
    11→- **Opcode 0x06** (pauseThread/BREAK) - OK
    12→- **Opcode 0x07** (JMP) - OK
    13→- **Opcode 0x08** (setVect) - OK
    14→- **Opcode 0x09** (DJNZ) - OK
    15→- **Opcode 0x0B** (setPalette) - OK
    16→- **Opcode 0x0D** (selectVideoPage) - OK
    17→- **Opcode 0x0E** (fillVideoPage) - OK
    18→- **Opcode 0x10** (blitFramebuffer) - OK (missing pause-slices timing, but functional)
    19→- **Opcode 0x11** (killThread) - OK
    20→- **Opcode 0x80** (video instruction high bit) - OK
    21→- Polygon rendering pipeline (readVertices, fillPolygon, calcStep, readAndDrawPolygonHierarchy) - OK
    22→- Thread scheduler (NEXT_THREAD, CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS) - OK
    23→- Video page management (GET_PAGE_PTR, UPDATE_DISPLAY, VIDEO_START) - OK
    24→- Character/string drawing - OK
    25→
    26→---
    27→
    28→### Critical Missing/Broken Items
    29→
    30→#### 1. **Opcode 0x01 (MOV) - BUG: doesn't actually copy the value**
    31→(`another_world_vm.asm:1148-1165`)
    32→
    33→The MOV instruction reads `srcVariableId` and `dstVariableId` but the write at line 1163 writes to `XIY` which still points to `VM_VARIABLES + srcVariableId`, not `dstVariableId`. The `POP WA` on line 1162 restores dstVariableId, but XIY is never recalculated to point at it. The variable index in XWA is never used to recompute the destination address.
    34→
    35→#### 2. **Opcode 0x02 (ADD) - BUG: same as MOV, doesn't add**
    36→(`another_world_vm.asm:1168-1186`)
    37→
    38→This is literally a copy of MOV's code. It reads the source value but never adds it to the destination. It should: read dst value, read src value, add them, write back to dst.
    39→
    40→#### 3. **Opcode 0x03 (addConst) - Endianness bug**
    41→(`another_world_vm.asm:1189-1203`)
    42→
    43→The `fetch_word()` at line 1199 reads 2 bytes from the bytecode. But the reference uses big-endian reads (`READ_WORD_AW` = `READ_BYTE(A) << 8 | READ_BYTE(A+1)`), while `LD WA, (XIX)` reads in native little-endian order. The bytecode is big-endian (Amiga/68k origin). **This same endianness issue likely affects all `fetch_word()` operations throughout the code** (opcodes 0x00, 0x03, 0x04, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, etc.).
    44→
    45→#### 4. **Opcode 0x0A (condJmp) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    46→(`another_world_vm.asm:1316-1325`)
    47→
    48→This just skips 5 bytes and does nothing. The conditional jump is essential for all game logic (branches, comparisons). Without it, the game can only run linear sequences. The reference has 6 comparison modes (eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le) plus variable-length operands depending on subopcode bits 6-7.
    49→
    50→#### 5. **Opcode 0x0C (resetThread) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    51→(`another_world_vm.asm:1339-1344`)
    52→
    53→Doesn't even consume its 3 bytes of arguments (first, last, type). This will desynchronize the bytecode parser, causing every subsequent instruction to decode incorrectly. The reference implementation freezes/unfreezes/deletes ranges of threads.
    54→
    55→#### 6. **Opcode 0x0F (copyVideoPage) - Ignores vscroll parameter**
    56→(`another_world_vm.asm:1379-1399`)
    57→
    58→The reference reads `VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y` and supports vertical scrolling with source/dest Y offsets. The KN5000 version does a plain memcpy. Also ignores the conditional `srcPageId & 0x80` / `srcPageId & 0xBF` logic for special scroll behavior.
    59→
    60→#### 7. **Opcode 0x12 (drawString) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    61→(`another_world_vm.asm:1427-1431`)
    62→
    63→Doesn't consume its 5 bytes of arguments (word stringId, byte x, byte y, byte color). Will desync the bytecode stream. The DRAW_STRING routine exists but is never called from here.
    64→
    65→#### 8. **Opcode 0x13 (SUB) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    66→(`another_world_vm.asm:1434-1439`)
    67→
    68→Doesn't consume its 2 bytes. Will desync.
    69→
    70→#### 9. **Opcode 0x14 (AND) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    71→(`another_world_vm.asm:1442-1447`)
    72→
    73→Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.
    74→
    75→#### 10. **Opcode 0x15 (OR) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    76→(`another_world_vm.asm:1450-1455`)
    77→
    78→Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.
    79→
    80→#### 11. **Opcode 0x16 (SHL) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    81→(`another_world_vm.asm:1458-1463`)
    82→
    83→Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.
    84→
    85→#### 12. **Opcode 0x17 (SHR) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    86→(`another_world_vm.asm:1466-1471`)
    87→
    88→Doesn't consume its 3 bytes. Will desync.
    89→
    90→#### 13. **Opcode 0x19 (LOAD/updateMemList) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    91→(`another_world_vm.asm:1484-1490`)
    92→
    93→Skips the word argument but does nothing. In the reference, this handles:
    94→- `resourceId == 0`: stop all sound
    95→- `resourceId > 0x91`: switch to a new game part (level change)
    96→- Otherwise: load a screen bitmap resource
    97→
    98→#### 14. **Opcode 0x40 (video with extended addressing) - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
    99→(`another_world_vm.asm:1072-1125`)
   100→
   101→The entire opcode 0x40 block is commented out and jumps to end without consuming any bytes. This handles polygon rendering with variable X/Y addressing modes and zoom. It's required for most in-game polygon graphics. **The variable-length encoding means skipping an unknown number of bytes, so this will definitely desync the VM.**
   102→
   103→#### 15. **drawLineP - NOT IMPLEMENTED (falls through to drawLineN)**
   104→(`another_world_vm.asm:89-102`)
   105→
   106→Should copy pixels from page_bitmaps[0] to curPagePtr1, but just draws solid color.
   107→
   108→#### 16. **drawLineBlend - NOT IMPLEMENTED (falls through to drawLineN)**
   109→(`another_world_vm.asm:104-117`)
   110→
   111→Should read the existing pixel and apply `(color & 7) | 8`, but just draws solid color.
   112→
   113→#### 17. **INPUT_UPDATE_PLAYER - NOT IMPLEMENTED**
   114→(`another_world_vm.asm:908-910`)
   115→
   116→Returns immediately. Without input handling, the game can never be interactive. The reference reads button/keyboard state and sets ~8 VM variables for hero movement, action, and mask.
   117→
   118→#### 18. **LOAD_SCREEN - Hardcoded to single bitmap**
   119→(`another_world_vm.asm:747-753`)
   120→
   121→Ignores the `screen_id` parameter entirely. The reference has 12 screen resources that get selected by index. Only one bitmap is ever loaded.
   122→
   123→#### 19. **Part/level switching not implemented**
   124→The reference has `initForPart()` / `setupPart()` which bank-switches bytecode, palettes, and video data when the game transitions between parts (intro, lake, jail, etc.). The KN5000 port hardcodes `INTRO_BYTECODE`, `INTRO_PALETTES`, `INTRO_VIDEO_1` labels, with no bank switching. `m_requestedNextPart` checking is commented out in `CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS`.
   125→
   126→#### 20. **VM hacks not implemented**
   127→The reference has several critical hacks:
   128→- `VM_HACK_SWITCH_FROM_INTRO_TO_LAKE`: Sets var 0xDC when transitioning from intro
   129→- `VM_HACK_INIT_VAR_54_WITH_81`: Required for the Interplay logo to show
   130→- `VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED`: Never initialized (noted as TODO on line 228)
   131→
   132→---
   133→
   134→### Summary by Severity
   135→
   136→**Will crash/desync the VM** (bytecode not consumed correctly):
   137→- Opcode 0x0C (resetThread) - missing 3 bytes
   138→- Opcode 0x12 (drawString) - missing 5 bytes
   139→- Opcode 0x13 (SUB) - missing 2 bytes
   140→- Opcode 0x14 (AND) - missing 3 bytes
   141→- Opcode 0x15 (OR) - missing 3 bytes
   142→- Opcode 0x16 (SHL) - missing 3 bytes
   143→- Opcode 0x17 (SHR) - missing 3 bytes
   144→- Opcode 0x40 (video extended) - variable length, unparsed
   145→- Opcode 0x0A (condJmp) - skips 5 bytes, but actual length is variable (5-6 bytes depending on subopcode)
   146→
   147→**Wrong behavior (logic bugs):**
   148→- Opcode 0x01 (MOV) - writes to wrong variable
   149→- Opcode 0x02 (ADD) - doesn't add, just copies (also to wrong dest)
   150→- Big-endian fetch_word not handled (affects most word-reading opcodes)
   151→
   152→**Missing but won't desync:**
   153→- Input handling
   154→- Part/level switching
   155→- Sound (understandable given hardware constraints)
   156→
   157→The port currently can only play the intro cinematic in a linear fashion (no branching, no interaction). To reach "complete and functional" status, the highest priority items would be: fixing the endianness issue, implementing condJmp (0x0A), fixing MOV/ADD, implementing the bytecode-consuming stubs to prevent desync, and then implementing opcode 0x40 for full polygon rendering.
   158→

1→# Debug Progress Report: Grey Screen Investigation
     2→
     3→**Date:** 2026-02-10
     4→**Previous session:** Fixed SETUP_PALETTE palette index extraction (commit 45ef21a)
     5→
     6→## Key Discovery: Grey Screen is Actually Correct Behavior
     7→
     8→The "light grey screen" is **not a bug** — it's the AW palette being applied correctly:
     9→
    10→- **Before setPalette:** VGA_Setup color 0 = (0,0,0) = pure black
    11→- **After setPalette(1):** Palette 1 color 0 = (4,4,4) in VGA DAC = very dark grey
    12→- The page buffers contain color index 0, so the screen shows dark grey
    13→
    14→**Proof:** Running 55 instructions (including setPalette), then resetting DAC color 0 to (0,0,0) → screen goes back to black. This confirms the palette write works correctly.
    15→
    16→## What Works
    17→
    18→1. **SETUP_PALETTE** — Fully functional. Correctly reads palette resource data, computes pointer offsets, extracts R/G/B nibbles, scales 4-bit to 6-bit, writes to VGA DAC with auto-increment. Verified with:
    19→   - All-black palette test → black ✓
    20→   - All-red palette test → red ✓
    21→   - Palette data pointer verification → reads correct byte (0x01) at palette 1 offset ✓
    22→   - Color 0 reset after setPalette → black ✓
    23→
    24→2. **VGA DAC writes** — Work correctly without delays (contrary to earlier hypothesis about bus timing)
    25→
    26→3. **VM execution** — Runs correctly through at least 55 instructions (thread scheduling, bytecode parsing, opcode dispatch all work)
    27→
    28→4. **condJmp (0x0A)** — Is fully implemented (despite code review saying otherwise). Variable-length encoding handled correctly (byte literal, 16-bit immediate, variable reference).
    29→
    30→## Actual Problem: No Polygon Content Visible
    31→
    32→The screen shows solid grey (correct palette color 0) but **no polygons or animations**. The VM continues executing but nothing gets drawn visibly.
    33→
    34→### Possible Causes (to investigate)
    35→
    36→1. **Polygon rendering hangs** — readAndDrawPolygon might enter an infinite loop on certain video data, halting VM execution
    37→
    38→2. **Bytecode desync from unimplemented opcodes** — Some opcodes might not consume the correct number of bytes. Need to verify ALL stubs consume correct byte counts.
    39→
    40→3. **Wrong page displayed** — Polygons might be drawn on a page that's never copied to VRAM by UPDATE_DISPLAY
    41→
    42→4. **Video data interpretation bugs** — The 0x80 opcode computes `offset = ((opcode << 8) | fetch_byte()) * 2` and indexes into INTRO_VIDEO_1. If the offset or data interpretation is wrong, polygon data would be garbage.
    43→
    44→5. **Page pointer corruption** — If CUR_PAGE_PTR_1 (draw target) points to the wrong memory, polygon fills write to incorrect locations
    45→
    46→### Immediate Next Steps
    47→
    48→1. **Check if VM is still running or hung** — Add a frame counter or visual indicator to UPDATE_DISPLAY to see if frames keep advancing after setPalette
    49→
    50→2. **Verify all opcode stubs consume correct bytes** — Audit every opcode handler for correct byte consumption, especially:
    51→   - 0x0C (resetThread) — 3 bytes
    52→   - 0x12 (drawString) — 5 bytes
    53→   - 0x13 (SUB) — 2 bytes
    54→   - 0x14 (AND) — 3 bytes
    55→   - 0x15 (OR) — 3 bytes
    56→   - 0x16 (SHL) — 3 bytes
    57→   - 0x17 (SHR) — 3 bytes
    58→
    59→3. **Check opcode 0x19 (LOAD)** — Some LOAD calls have resourceId > 0x91 which should trigger part switching. If the stub doesn't handle this, the VM might try to switch to unavailable parts.
    60→
    61→4. **Test if polygon rendering actually executes** — Add a visual indicator inside readAndDrawPolygon to confirm it's being called
    62→
    63→## Binary Search Results (with proper PUSH/POP counter preservation)
    64→
    65→| Instructions | Result | Notes |
    66→|---|---|---|
    67→| 10 | Black | Correct |
    68→| 50 | Black | Correct |
    69→| 52 | Black | Correct |
    70→| 53 | Black | Correct |

    72→| 55 | Grey | setPalette(1) changes color 0 to dark grey |

428→ENTRY:
   429→	EI 0 ; Enable interrupts (INTT1 timer ISR)
   430→
   431→	CALL GAME_RESET
   432→
   433→	; Initialize frame start time
   434→	LD XWA, (SYSTEM_TICKS)
   435→	LD (FRAME_START_TICKS), XWA
   436→
   437→MAIN_LOOP:
   438→	CALL EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
   439→	JP MAIN_LOOP
   440→
   441→LONG_PAUSE:
   442→	LD BC, 0
   443→LONG_PAUSE_LOOP1:
   444→	LD DE, 080h
   445→LONG_PAUSE_LOOP2:
   446→	DJNZ DE, LONG_PAUSE_LOOP2
   447→	DJNZ BC, LONG_PAUSE_LOOP1
   448→	RET
   449→
   450→PAUSE:
   451→	; Timer-based frame delay using VM variable 0xFF (pause slices).
   452→	; Each slice = ~20ms. Polls SYSTEM_TICKS until elapsed >= target.
   453→	; DJNZ fallback counter exits if timer ISR doesn't fire.
   454→
   455→	; Read VM variable 0xFF (pause slices)
   456→	LD A, 0FFh
   457→	CALL _read_vm_var		; DE = var[0xFF]
   458→
   459→	; Cap slices at 1-5 range
   460→	LD A, E
   461→	CP A, 0
   462→	JP NE, _pause_nonzero
   463→	LD A, 1
   464→_pause_nonzero:
   465→	CP A, 6
   466→	JP ULT, _pause_capped
   467→	LD A, 5
   468→_pause_capped:
   469→	; Compute target_ticks = slices * TICKS_PER_SLICE
   470→	LD D, 0
   471→	LD E, A					; DE = capped slices (1-5)
   472→	LD WA, TICKS_PER_SLICE	; WA = 250
   473→	MUL XWA, DE			; XWA = target_ticks (16-bit result in WA)
   474→	LD XBC, XWA			; XBC = target_ticks (preserved across loop)
   475→
   476→	; Check for overrun: elapsed already >= target?
   477→	LD XWA, (SYSTEM_TICKS)
   478→	LD XDE, (FRAME_START_TICKS)
   479→	SUB XWA, XDE			; XWA = elapsed ticks
   480→	CP XWA, XBC
   481→	JP UGE, _pause_overrun
   482→
   483→	; Poll timer with DJNZ fallback (65536 iterations ≈ 80ms safety net)
   484→	LD HL, 0				; fallback counter
   485→_pause_wait:
   486→	LD XWA, (SYSTEM_TICKS)
   487→	LD XDE, (FRAME_START_TICKS)
   488→	SUB XWA, XDE			; XWA = elapsed
   489→	CP XWA, XBC
   490→	JP UGE, _pause_done_ok
   491→	DJNZ HL, _pause_wait
   492→	; Fallback expired — exit (timer may not be running)
   493→
   494→_pause_done_ok:
   495→	LD (LAST_FRAME_TICKS), WA
   496→	LDB (FRAME_OVERRAN), 0
   497→	RET
   498→
   499→_pause_overrun:
   500→	LD (LAST_FRAME_TICKS), WA
   501→	LDB (FRAME_OVERRAN), 1
   502→	RET

```
Part 0 (0x03E80): Protection     - Code wheel entry, splash screens
Part 1 (0x03E81): Intro          - Introduction cinematic
Part 2 (0x03E82): Water          - Lake level
Part 3 (0x03E83): Jail           - Prison level
Part 4 (0x03E84): Citadel        - Castle level
Part 5 (0x03E85): Battlechar     - Battle cinematic
Part 6 (0x03E86): Arena          - Arena level
Part 7 (0x03E87): Final          - Ending
Part 8 (0x03E88): Password1      - Password entry screen
Part 9 (0x03E89): Password2      - Password entry (alternate)
```

Each part has up to 4 resources loaded dynamically:
```asm
PART_RESOURCE_TABLE:
    ; Each entry: [palette (DD), bytecode (DD), video1 (DD), video2 (DD)]
    ; Part 0: Protection
    dd PART0_PALETTES, PART0_BYTECODE, PART0_VIDEO_1, 0
    ; Part 1: Intro
    dd PART1_PALETTES, PART1_BYTECODE, PART1_VIDEO_1, 0
    ; Part 2: Water (uses shared video2)
    dd PART2_PALETTES, PART2_BYTECODE, PART2_VIDEO_1, SHARED_VIDEO_2
    ; ... more parts
```

### **The `initForPart` Subroutine: Core of Part Switching**

Located at line 271 in `another_world_vm.asm`, this is the **critical function** for all part transitions:

```asm
initForPart:
    Input: WA = partId (0x03E80 through 0x03E89)
    Effect: Completely reinitialize the VM for a new game part
    
    Steps:
    1. Store partId in CURRENT_PART_ID (memory variable)
    2. Reset VM_STACK to start address
    3. LOOP over all 64 threads:
       - Set PC = INACTIVE_THREAD (thread disabled)
       - Set REQUESTED_PC = NO_REQUEST (0xFFFF)
       - Set CURRENT_STATE = NOT_FROZEN
       - Set REQUESTED_STATE = NO_STATE_REQUEST
    4. Enable thread 0 at PC=0 (bytecode entry point)
    5. Load 4 resource pointers from PART_RESOURCE_TABLE:
       - Compute table offset = (partId - GAME_PART_FIRST) * 16
       - Read: palette_ptr, bytecode_ptr, video1_ptr, video2_ptr
       - Store in: CUR_PALETTES, CUR_BYTECODE, CUR_VIDEO_DATA, CUR_VIDEO_2
    6. Set vm_var[0xE4] = 0x14 (reference compatibility)
    7. Return (thread 0 now running new bytecode)
```

#### **Phase 1: Hardware Initialization (line 333)**
```asm
CALL VIDEO_START
```

#### **Phase 2: VM State Reset (lines 336-374)**
- Zero all 256 VM variables (256 × 16-bit = 512 bytes)
- Initialize all threads as INACTIVE
- Set stack pointer
- Set thread 0 PC = 0 (entry point)

This is the **critical protection bypass** - sets variables the protection code would set:
```asm
var[0xBC] = 0x0010         ; Protection check #1
var[0xF2] = 0x0FA0         ; Protection check #2  
var[0xDC] = 0x0021         ; Protection check #3 (VM hack by ref)
var[0x54] = 0x0081         ; Interplay logo requirement
```

The water part (Part 2) checks at subroutine 0x009A whether `var[0xBC] & 0x0010 && var[0xF2] == 0x0FA0 && var[0xDC] == 0x21`. If all are true, protection is "passed" and the game continues. Otherwise, all threads die and game halts.

```asm
LDW (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), 0        ; No part switch yet
LD WA, GAME_PART_PROTECTION         ; WA = 0x03E80
CALL initForPart                      ; Initialize Part 0
LDW (THREADS_DATA + PC_OFFSET), 0x007B  ; OVERRIDE: Skip code wheel
```

**Critical detail:** The bytecode entry at PC=0 goes to the code wheel (user input). Since we can't interact, we override the thread 0 PC to 0x007B, which is the splash screen entry point (after code wheel validation).

#### **Phase 5: Start Display Loop (lines 417-424)**
```asm
; Thread 60 is the main display/game loop thread (from original bytecode design)
; Original bytecode at 0x010A3 sets up the loop
LDW (THREADS_DATA + (60 * 4) + PC_OFFSET), 0x010A3
LD A, 0FFh
LD DE, 2
CALL _write_vm_var          ; var[0xFF] = 2 (frame pause slices)
```

The flow is:
1. Part 0 plays: splash screens (Interplay logo, credits, code wheel bypass)
2. Part 0 bytecode eventually executes `LOAD` opcode with resourceId > 0x91
3. This sets `REQUESTED_NEXT_PART` to Part 1 (Intro)
4. Next frame, `CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS` (line 1389) validates and calls `initForPart(PART1)`
5. Part 1's bytecode loads and threads run from thread 0 PC=0
6. Intro cinematic plays

### **The Part Switch Opcode (0x19 LOAD)**

Located at line 2461, handles both resource loading and part switching:

```asm
LOAD:
    Input: resourceId (16-bit, big-endian from bytecode)
    
    Cases:
    - resourceId == 0:
        Stop sound (no-op in KN5000)
    - resourceId > 0x91 (> NUM_MEM_LIST):
        REQUESTED_NEXT_PART = resourceId
        (will be processed by CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS on next frame)
    - Otherwise (0x01 to 0x91):
        Load screen bitmap (0x12, 0x13, 0x47, 0x49, 0x53)
        or unknown resource (no-op)
```

### **Frame-Boundary Part Switch Logic**

`CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS` (line 1389):
```asm
1. Read REQUESTED_NEXT_PART
2. If non-zero:
   a. Validate: GAME_PART_FIRST <= partId <= GAME_PART_LAST
   b. Call initForPart(partId) to reinitialize everything
   c. Set REQUESTED_NEXT_PART = 0 (clear request)
3. Then process all thread state changes (freeze/unfreeze/delete)
```

This ensures:
- Part switches only happen at frame boundaries
- All threads are properly cleaned up before new part loads
- No mid-frame resource conflicts

1. **Two-stage VM_PC update:**
   - `_end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION`: Recompute VM_PC from XIX offset after instruction
   - `_after_PC_update`: Skip recomputation (used by JMP, CALL, RET, NEXT_THREAD, part-switch-aware opcodes)

   palette_ptr = PART_RESOURCE_TABLE[index + 0]
   bytecode_ptr = PART_RESOURCE_TABLE[index + 4]
   video1_ptr = PART_RESOURCE_TABLE[index + 8]
   video2_ptr = PART_RESOURCE_TABLE[index + 12]
   ```

All part-related state resides in RAM (starting at 0x010000 on MAINCPU or 0x200000 on EXTENSION):

```

    var[0x54] = Interplay logo display flag
    var[0xBC] = Protection check #1
    var[0xDC] = Protection check #3
    var[0xF2] = Protection check #2

CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS:

	; Check if a part switch has been requested
	LD WA, (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART)
	CP WA, 0
	JP EQ, _no_part_switch

	; Validate part ID range before switching
	CP WA, GAME_PART_FIRST
	JP ULT, _invalid_part_switch
	CP WA, GAME_PART_LAST
	JP UGT, _invalid_part_switch

	; Part switch requested - call initForPart (WA = partId)
	CALL initForPart
_invalid_part_switch:
	LDW (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), 0
_no_part_switch:

	LD A, 0
_check_thread_reqs__loop:

	; thread->state = thread->requested_state;
	; After applying, clear requested_state to NOT_FROZEN.
	; This matches the reference HLE where requested_state is a bool
	; and "= NO_REQUEST" (0xFFFF) truncates to true (UNFROZEN).
	; Effect: FREEZE is one-shot (lasts one frame, then auto-unfreezes).
	; This is critical for the death handler which FREEZEs all threads
	; then sets up threads 0 and 60 — without auto-unfreeze, they
	; stay frozen and the password display never runs.
	PUSH WA
	SLA 1, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
	LD E, (XWA + REQUESTED_STATE)
	CP E, NO_STATE_REQUEST
	JP EQ, _no_state_request
	LD (XWA + CURRENT_STATE), E
	LD (XWA + REQUESTED_STATE), NOT_FROZEN	; clear request (auto-unfreeze)
_no_state_request:
	POP WA

	PUSH WA
	SLA 2, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, THREADS_DATA
	LD DE, (XWA + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET)
	POP WA
	CP DE, NO_REQUEST
	JP EQ, _check_thread_reqs__next_loop

	PUSH WA
	SLA 2, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, THREADS_DATA
	LD BC, (XWA + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET)
	CP DE, DELETE_THIS_THREAD
	JP NE, _dont_delete_this_thread
	LD BC, INACTIVE_THREAD
_dont_delete_this_thread:
	LDW (XWA + PC_OFFSET), BC
	LDW (XWA + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), NO_REQUEST
	POP WA

_check_thread_reqs__next_loop:
	INC A
	CP A, 64
	JP NE, _check_thread_reqs__loop

_end_of__check_thread_reqs:
	RET

	DJNZ BC, children_loop
	RET


LOAD_SCREEN:
; Input: XHL = pointer to 32000 bytes of 4bpp Amiga planar screen data
; Converts to 8bpp chunky and writes 64000 bytes to PAGE_BITMAP_0
; Planar format: 4 bitplanes x 8000 bytes (320x200 / 8 bits per byte)
; Each source byte produces 8 destination pixels.
; Clobbers: XWA, XBC, XDE, XHL; preserves XIX
	PUSH XIX

	LD (BMP_SRC_PTR), XHL		; save source base pointer
	LD XDE, PAGE_BITMAP_0		; destination: page 0 buffer
	LD IX, 8000					; outer loop: 8000 byte positions

_bmp_outer:
	; Load one byte from each of the 4 bitplanes
	LD XHL, (BMP_SRC_PTR)
	LD A, (XHL)					; plane 0 (bit 0 of pixel color)
	PUSH XHL
	ADD XHL, 8000
	LD B, (XHL)					; plane 1 (bit 1)
	ADD XHL, 8000
	LD C, (XHL)					; plane 2 (bit 2)
	ADD XHL, 8000
	LD W, (XHL)					; plane 3 (bit 3)
	POP XHL
	INC XHL
	LD (BMP_SRC_PTR), XHL		; advance source pointer

	; Convert 8 pixels from MSB to LSB
	; A=plane0, B=plane1, C=plane2, W=plane3
	LD H, 8						; pixel counter (8 pixels per byte)
_bmp_pixel:
	LD L, 0
	; Extract MSB from each plane (p3 first → bit 3 of pixel)
	SLA 1, W					; plane 3 MSB → carry
	RLC L						; carry → L bit 0
	SLA 1, C					; plane 2 MSB → carry
	RLC L						; carry → L bit 0, prev → bit 1
	SLA 1, B					; plane 1 MSB → carry
	RLC L						; carry → L bit 0
	SLA 1, A					; plane 0 MSB → carry
	RLC L						; L = (p3<<3)|(p2<<2)|(p1<<1)|p0
	LD (XDE), L
	INC XDE
	DJNZ H, _bmp_pixel

	DJNZ IX, _bmp_outer

	POP XIX
	RET

SETUP_PALETTE:
	; WA: palette index (0-63), already extracted by caller (opcode 0x0B does SRA 8)
	; XWA: zero-extended by caller (EXTZ XWA)
	; Palette format: 2 bytes per color, 0x0RGB (4 bits per channel)
	; Byte 0: 0000_RRRR (low nibble = red)
	; Byte 1: GGGG_BBBB (high nibble = green, low nibble = blue)

	; Compute byte offset: palette_index * 32
	SLA 1, WA			; * 2
	SLA 4, WA			; * 16 → total * 32 (each palette = 16 colors × 2 bytes)

GAME_RESET:
	CALL VIDEO_START

	; Zero all VM variables (256 x 16-bit = 512 bytes)
	LD XDE, VM_VARIABLES
	LD WA, 0
	LD BC, 256
_zero_vars_loop:
	LD (XDE), WA
	INC 2, XDE
	DJNZ BC, _zero_vars_loop

	LDB (CURRENT_THREAD), 0
	LDW (VM_PC), 0
	LD XIX, VM_STACK
	LD (VM_STACK_POINTER), XIX

	; All threads are initially disabled and unfrozen
	LD IX, 0
_setup_threads__loop:

	PUSH IX
	SLA 2, IX
	EXTZ XIX
	ADD XIX, THREADS_DATA
	LDW (XIX + PC_OFFSET), INACTIVE_THREAD
	LDW (XIX + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), NO_REQUEST
	POP IX

	PUSH IX
	SLA 1, IX
	EXTZ XIX
	ADD XIX, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
	LD (XIX + CURRENT_STATE), NOT_FROZEN
	LD (XIX + REQUESTED_STATE), NO_STATE_REQUEST
	POP IX

	INC IX
	CP IX, 64
	JP NE, _setup_threads__loop

	; Start thread 0 at PC=0 (matching initForPart behavior)
	LDW (THREADS_DATA + PC_OFFSET), 0

	; Initialize VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED with a fixed seed (no RTC available)
	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_RANDOM_SEED
	LD DE, 1234h			; Fixed seed value
	CALL _write_vm_var

	; VM_HACK_INIT_VAR_54_WITH_81: Required for Interplay logo display
	LD A, 054h
	LD DE, 0081h
	CALL _write_vm_var

	; Copy protection bypass: Set the variables that the protection
	; bytecode (resource 0x15) would set when the correct code wheel
	; answer is entered. Without these, the water part's check at
	; subroutine 0x009A kills all threads and the game halts.
	; Protection check requires: var[0xBC] & 0x0010, var[0xF2] == 0x0FA0,
	; var[0xDC] == 0x21. These are set by the protection code at offsets
	; 0x0CCF (OR var[0xBC] |= 0x0010), 0x0D0D (var[0xF2] = 0x0FA0),
	; and indirectly via the VM hack (var[0xDC] = 0x21).
	LD A, 0BCh
	LD DE, 0010h
	CALL _write_vm_var
	LD A, 0F2h
	LD DE, 0FA0h
	CALL _write_vm_var
	LD A, 0DCh
	LD DE, 021h
	CALL _write_vm_var

	; Initialize part tracking and start from the protection/splash screens
	; (Part 0 = logo, credits, code-wheel). We bypass the code wheel by
	; starting thread 0 at the splash screen entry point (0x007B) instead
	; of PC=0 (which enters the code wheel). We also pre-start the display
	; loop thread and set the frame delay variable, matching what the
	; bytecode's normal entry at 0x0000 would have done.
	LDW (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), 0
	LD WA, GAME_PART_PROTECTION
	CALL initForPart

	; Override thread 0 PC to splash screen entry (skip code wheel at 0x0000)
	LDW (THREADS_DATA + PC_OFFSET), 007Bh

	; Start display loop on thread 60 (bytecode address 0x10A3)
	; Thread 60 slot = 60 * 4 = 240 bytes into THREADS_DATA
	LDW (THREADS_DATA + (60 * 4) + PC_OFFSET), 010A3h

	; Set var[0xFF] = 2 (frame delay, normally set by bytecode at 0x0003)
	LD A, 0FFh
	LD DE, 2
	CALL _write_vm_var

	RET

ENTRY:
	EI 0 ; Enable interrupts (INTT1 timer ISR)

ENTRY:
	EI 0 ; Enable interrupts (INTT1 timer ISR)

	CALL GAME_RESET

	; Initialize frame start time
	LD XWA, (SYSTEM_TICKS)
	LD (FRAME_START_TICKS), XWA

MAIN_LOOP:
	CALL EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
	JP MAIN_LOOP

LONG_PAUSE:
	LD BC, 0
LONG_PAUSE_LOOP1:
	LD DE, 080h
LONG_PAUSE_LOOP2:
	DJNZ DE, LONG_PAUSE_LOOP2
	DJNZ BC, LONG_PAUSE_LOOP1
	RET

PAUSE:
	; Timer-based frame delay using VM variable 0xFF (pause slices).
	; Each slice = ~20ms. Polls SYSTEM_TICKS until elapsed >= target.
	; DJNZ fallback counter exits if timer ISR doesn't fire.

	; Read VM variable 0xFF (pause slices)
	LD A, 0FFh
	CALL _read_vm_var		; DE = var[0xFF]

ADD XIY, XWA
	LD (XIY), DE
	RET


	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
; _cpanel_send_byte: Send/receive one byte via SC1 synchronous I/O
; In sync mode, writing SC1BUF simultaneously sends and receives.
; Input: A = byte to send
; Output: A = byte received
; Clobbers: A only (W preserved)
_cpanel_send_byte:
	LD (SC1BUF), A			; Start 8-bit transfer
	LD A, 0FFh				; Delay ~255 iterations (~95µs at 16 MHz > 64µs @ 125 kHz effective SCLK)
.delay:
	DEC 1, A
	JR NZ, .delay
	LD A, (SC1BUF)			; Read received byte
	RET

; _cpanel_query_segment: Query a control panel button segment
; Input: B = command (0x20=left panel, 0xE0=right panel), C = segment number
; Output: A = button bitmap
; Clobbers: A, W
_cpanel_query_segment:
	LD A, B					; Send command byte
	CALL _cpanel_send_byte
	LD A, C					; Send segment byte
	CALL _cpanel_send_byte
	LD A, 0FFh				; Send dummy (clock in header)
	CALL _cpanel_send_byte	; A = header (discard)
	LD A, 0FFh				; Send dummy (clock in bitmap)
	CALL _cpanel_send_byte	; A = button bitmap
	RET
	endif ; TARGET_MAINCPU

INPUT_UPDATE_PLAYER:
	ifdef TARGET_MAINCPU
	; Query CPR_SEG4 (right panel segment 4) for direction buttons
	; CPR_SEG4: bit1=UP(PART:RIGHT2), bit4=LEFT(CONDUCTOR:LEFT),
	;           bit5=DOWN(CONDUCTOR:RIGHT2), bit6=RIGHT(CONDUCTOR:RIGHT1)
	LD B, 0E0h				; Right panel command
	LD C, 004h				; Segment 4
	CALL _cpanel_query_segment
	LD H, A					; H = CPR_SEG4 bitmap

	; Query CPL_SEG4 (left panel segment 4) for action button
	; CPL_SEG4: bit3=ACTION(VARIATION 4)
	LD B, 020h				; Left panel command
	; C still = 004h
	CALL _cpanel_query_segment
	LD L, A					; L = CPL_SEG4 bitmap

	; Build lr (left/right), ud (up/down), and mask m
	; H, L, C are preserved across _write_vm_var (only clobbers XIY, XWA)
	LD C, 0					; C = mask accumulator (m)

	; --- RIGHT (H bit 6 = CONDUCTOR:RIGHT1) ---
	LD DE, 0				; lr = 0
	BIT 6, H
	JR Z, .no_right
	LD DE, 1				; lr = 1
	SET 0, C				; m |= 1 (right)
.no_right:

	; --- LEFT (H bit 4 = CONDUCTOR:LEFT) ---
	BIT 4, H
	JR Z, .no_left
	LD DE, -1				; lr = -1
	SET 1, C				; m |= 2 (left)
.no_left:

	; Write VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_LEFT_RIGHT = lr (DE)
	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_LEFT_RIGHT
	CALL _write_vm_var

	; --- DOWN (H bit 5 = CONDUCTOR:RIGHT2) ---
	LD DE, 0				; ud = 0
	BIT 5, H
	JR Z, .no_down
	LD DE, 1				; ud = 1
	SET 2, C				; m |= 4 (down)
.no_down:

	; --- UP (H bit 1 = PART:RIGHT2) ---
	BIT 1, H
	JR Z, .no_up
	LD DE, -1				; ud = -1
	SET 3, C				; m |= 8 (up)
	; UP pressed: write HERO_POS_UP_DOWN = -1
	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_UP_DOWN
	CALL _write_vm_var		; DE = -1
	JR .up_down_done
.no_up:
	; UP not pressed: write HERO_POS_UP_DOWN = ud (0 or 1)
	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_UP_DOWN
	CALL _write_vm_var		; DE = ud

.up_down_done:
	; Write VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_JUMP_DOWN = ud (DE still = ud)
	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_JUMP_DOWN
	CALL _write_vm_var

	; Write VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_MASK = m
	LD D, 0
	LD E, C					; DE = m (zero-extended)
	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_POS_MASK
	CALL _write_vm_var

	; --- ACTION (L bit 3 = VARIATION 4) ---
	LD DE, 0				; button = 0
	BIT 3, L
	JR Z, .no_action
	LD DE, 1				; button = 1
	SET 7, C				; m |= 0x80 (action)
.no_action:

	; Write VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION = button
	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION
	CALL _write_vm_var

	; Write VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION_POS_MASK = m (with action bit)
	LD D, 0
	LD E, C					; DE = m
	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_HERO_ACTION_POS_MASK
	CALL _write_vm_var

	RET

	else ; TARGET_EXTENSION

; ====  COPY_VIDEO_PAGE instruction  ====
	CP A, 0Fh
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_COPY_VIDEO_PAGE
	LD B, (XIX)		; byte srcPageId
	INC XIX
	LD C, (XIX)		; byte dstPageId
	INC XIX

	; Get destination page pointer
	LD A, C
	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
	PUSH XWA		; save dst pointer on stack

	; Check for simple copy: srcPageId >= 0xFE
	CP B, 0FEh
	JP UGE, _copypage_simple

	; Check scroll mode: (srcPageId & 0xBF) has bit 7 set?
	LD A, B
	AND A, 0BFh
	BIT 7, A
	JP Z, _copypage_simple_masked

	; === Scroll mode ===
	; Actual source page = srcPageId & 3
	AND A, 3
	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
	LD XDE, XWA		; XDE = src page base

	; Read vscroll from VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y
	PUSH XDE		; save src base
	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y
	CALL _read_vm_var	; DE = vscroll (16-bit signed)
	LD HL, DE		; HL = vscroll
	POP XDE			; restore src base

	; Validate: -199 <= vscroll <= 199
	CP HL, -199
	JP LT, _copypage_scroll_skip
	CP HL, 199
	JP GT, _copypage_scroll_skip

	; Compute h, src_y0, dest_y0
	LD BC, 200		; h = screen height
	POP XWA			; XWA = dst base
	PUSH XWA		; re-push for later pop

	CP HL, 0
	JP GE, _copypage_vscroll_positive

	; vscroll < 0: h += vscroll, src_y0 = -vscroll
	ADD BC, HL		; h += vscroll (vscroll is negative)
	LD WA, 0
	SUB WA, HL		; WA = -vscroll = src_y0
	; Advance src pointer by src_y0 * 320
	PUSH BC
	LD BC, 320
	EXTZ XWA
	MUL XWA, BC
	ADD XDE, XWA	; src += src_y0 * 320
	POP BC
	JP _copypage_do_scroll

_copypage_vscroll_positive:
	; vscroll >= 0: h -= vscroll, dest_y0 = vscroll
	SUB BC, HL		; h -= vscroll
	LD WA, HL		; WA = vscroll = dest_y0
	; Advance dst pointer by dest_y0 * 320
	POP XHL			; XHL = dst base (from stack)
	PUSH BC
	LD BC, 320
	EXTZ XWA
	MUL XWA, BC
	ADD XHL, XWA	; dst += dest_y0 * 320
	POP BC
	PUSH XHL		; re-push adjusted dst

_copypage_do_scroll:
	; Copy h scanlines (BC = h, XDE = src, stack top = dst)
	POP XHL			; XHL = dst pointer
	; Convert h scanlines to dword count: h * 320 / 4 = h * 80
	LD WA, BC		; WA = h
	EXTZ XWA
	LD BC, 80
	MUL XWA, BC		; XWA = h * 80
	LD BC, WA		; BC = dword count
_copypage_scroll_loop:
	LD XWA, (XDE)
	LD (XHL), XWA
	INC 4, XDE
	INC 4, XHL
	DJNZ BC, _copypage_scroll_loop
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION

_copypage_scroll_skip:
	POP XWA			; clean up stack (dst pointer)
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION

_copypage_simple_masked:
	; srcPageId after masking still doesn't have bit 7 set - use masked value
	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
	LD XDE, XWA
	JP _copypage_do_simple

_copypage_simple:
	; Simple copy: get src page from original srcPageId
	LD A, B
	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
	LD XDE, XWA

_copypage_do_simple:
	POP XHL			; XHL = dst page pointer (from stack)
	LD BC, 320 * 200 / 4
_copy_videopage_loop:
	LD XWA, (XDE)
	LD (XHL), XWA
	INC 4, XDE
	INC 4, XHL
	DJNZ BC, _copy_videopage_loop
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_COPY_VIDEO_PAGE:

	CP A, 10h

	BIT 6, B

	EX W, A			; byte-swap: bytecode is big-endian
	LD BC, WA		; BC = jump offset

	LD A, B
	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
	LD XDE, XWA

_copypage_do_simple:
	POP XHL			; XHL = dst page pointer (from stack)
	LD BC, 320 * 200 / 4
_copy_videopage_loop:
	LD XWA, (XDE)
	LD (XHL), XWA
	INC 4, XDE
	INC 4, XHL
	DJNZ BC, _copy_videopage_loop
	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION
INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_COPY_VIDEO_PAGE:


	; ====  BLIT_FRAMEBUFFER instruction  ====
	CP A, 10h
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_BLIT_FRAMEBUFFER
	LD A, (XIX)		; byte pageId
	INC XIX

	; VM_HACK_SWITCH_FROM_INTRO_TO_LAKE:
	; If currentPart == PROTECTION and vm_var[0x67] == 1, set vm_var[0xDC] = 0x21
	; (The protection bytecode sets var[0x67]=1 when correct answer is entered;
	; this hack then sets var[0xDC]=0x21 which subsequent parts check.)
	; Note: Since we skip protection and set var[0xDC] directly in GAME_RESET,
	; this hack is currently redundant, but kept for correctness.
	PUSH WA			; save pageId
	LD WA, (CURRENT_PART_ID)
	CP WA, GAME_PART_PROTECTION
	JP NE, _blit_no_hack
	LD A, 067h
	CALL _read_vm_var	; DE = vm_var[0x67]
	CP DE, 1
	JP NE, _blit_no_hack
	LD A, 0DCh
	LD DE, 021h
	CALL _write_vm_var

	POP WA			; restore pageId (A = pageId)
	CALL UPDATE_DISPLAY
	CALL PAUSE			; Frame timing delay

	LDB (001a0000h + 20*320 + 319), 00h	; color 0 (background)

	JP _end_of_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION

	LD WA, 0

CHECK_THREAD_REQUESTS:

	; Check if a part switch has been requested
	LD WA, (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART)
	CP WA, 0
	JP EQ, _no_part_switch

	; Validate part ID range before switching
	CP WA, GAME_PART_FIRST
	JP ULT, _invalid_part_switch
	CP WA, GAME_PART_LAST
	JP UGT, _invalid_part_switch

	; Part switch requested - call initForPart (WA = partId)
	CALL initForPart
_invalid_part_switch:
	LDW (REQUESTED_NEXT_PART), 0
_no_part_switch:

	LD A, 0
_check_thread_reqs__loop:

	; thread->state = thread->requested_state;
	; After applying, clear requested_state to NOT_FROZEN.
	; This matches the reference HLE where requested_state is a bool
	; and "= NO_REQUEST" (0xFFFF) truncates to true (UNFROZEN).
	; Effect: FREEZE is one-shot (lasts one frame, then auto-unfreezes).
	; This is critical for the death handler which FREEZEs all threads
	; then sets up threads 0 and 60 — without auto-unfreeze, they
	; stay frozen and the password display never runs.
	PUSH WA
	SLA 1, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, VM_IS_CHANNEL_ACTIVE
	LD E, (XWA + REQUESTED_STATE)
	CP E, NO_STATE_REQUEST

	LD (XWA + CURRENT_STATE), E
	LD (XWA + REQUESTED_STATE), NOT_FROZEN	; clear request (auto-unfreeze)

	POP WA

	SLA 2, WA
	EXTZ XWA
	ADD XWA, THREADS_DATA

	CP DE, DELETE_THIS_THREAD
	JP NE, _dont_delete_this_thread
	LD BC, INACTIVE_THREAD
_dont_delete_this_thread:
	LDW (XWA + PC_OFFSET), BC
	LDW (XWA + REQUESTED_PC_OFFSET), NO_REQUEST
	POP WA

_check_thread_reqs__next_loop:
	INC A
	CP A, 64
	JP NE, _check_thread_reqs__loop

_end_of__check_thread_reqs:
	RET

CP A, 0Fh
	JP NE, INSTRUCTION_IS_NOT_COPY_VIDEO_PAGE
	LD B, (XIX)		; byte srcPageId
	INC XIX
	LD C, (XIX)		; byte dstPageId
	INC XIX

	LD A, C
	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
	PUSH XWA		; save dst pointer on stack

	; Check for simple copy: srcPageId >= 0xFE
	CP B, 0FEh
	JP UGE, _copypage_simple

	; Check scroll mode: (srcPageId & 0xBF) has bit 7 set?
	LD A, B
	AND A, 0BFh
	BIT 7, A
	JP Z, _copypage_simple_masked

	; === Scroll mode ===
	; Actual source page = srcPageId & 3
	AND A, 3
	CALL GET_PAGE_PTR
	LD XDE, XWA		; XDE = src page base

	; Read vscroll from VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y
	PUSH XDE		; save src base
	LD A, VM_VARIABLE_SCROLL_Y
	CALL _read_vm_var	; DE = vscroll (16-bit signed)
	LD HL, DE		; HL = vscroll
	POP XDE			; restore src base

	; Validate: -199 <= vscroll <= 199
	CP HL, -199
	JP LT, _copypage_scroll_skip
	CP HL, 199
	JP GT, _copypage_scroll_skip

	; Compute h, src_y0, dest_y0
	LD BC, 200		; h = screen height
	POP XWA			; XWA = dst base
	PUSH XWA		; re-push for later pop

	CP HL, 0
	JP GE, _copypage_vscroll_positive

	; vscroll < 0: h += vscroll, src_y0 = -vscroll
	ADD BC, HL		; h += vscroll (vscroll is negative)
	LD WA, 0
	SUB WA, HL		; WA = -vscroll = src_y0
	; Advance src pointer by src_y0 * 320
	PUSH BC
	LD BC, 320
	EXTZ XWA
	MUL XWA, BC
	ADD XDE, XWA	; src += src_y0 * 320
	POP BC
	JP _copypage_do_scroll

_copypage_vscroll_positive:
	; vscroll >= 0: h -= vscroll, dest_y0 = vscroll
	SUB BC, HL		; h -= vscroll
	LD WA, HL		; WA = vscroll = dest_y0
	; Advance dst pointer by dest_y0 * 320
	POP XHL			; XHL = dst base (from stack)
	PUSH BC
	LD BC, 320
	EXTZ XWA
	MUL XWA, BC
	ADD XHL, XWA	; dst += dest_y0 * 320

_copypage_do_scroll:
	; Copy h scanlines (BC = h, XDE = src, stack top = dst)
	POP XHL			; XHL = dst pointer

	LD WA, BC		; WA = h
	EXTZ XWA
	LD BC, 80
	MUL XWA, BC		; XWA = h * 80
	LD BC, WA		; BC = dword count
_copypage_scroll_loop:
	LD XWA, (XDE)
	LD (XHL), XWA
	INC 4, XDE
	INC 4, XHL
	DJNZ BC, _copypage_scroll_loop

**Bypass flow** (PC starts at 0x007B):

- 0x007F: if var[0x54] < 0x0080 → JUMP 0x00BF (condition FALSE since 0x80 >= 0x80, continue)

- 0x0165: AND var[0x54] &= 0x0001 → var[0x54] = 0x0080 & 0x0001 = 0x0000
